item.title: New legislation tabled to replace IRAC with modern, transparent, and specialized regulators built for Islanders
item.description:
New legislation tabled to replace IRAC with modern, transparent, and specialized regulators built for Islanders jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/18/2026 - 16:26

The Government of Prince Edward Island has tabled the Appeals, Land and Regulatory Commission of Prince Edward Island Act to replace the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission with two new specialized boards: the PEI Energy and Utilities Board and the PEI Land and Appeals Board, which is supported by a shared administrative body which will be known as the Appeals, Land and Regulatory Commission.

“Islanders deserve a regulatory system that is fair, transparent and accountable, and that works for the people who rely on it. Commissioner Francis has given us a clear path forward, and we’re taking the steps needed to put these changes into place. This is significant work, and we’re committed to doing it properly while protecting the independence of the decisions these bodies make.”    

- Premier Rob Lantz  

The Bill puts into law the foundational recommendations of the Independent Review of the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission, led by Commissioner Rory Francis.  The final report was delivered on November 1, 2026, and contains 74 recommendations after months of engagement with Islanders, municipalities, industry and subject-matter experts.     

Through various bills now tabled in the Legislative Assembly, government is advancing a number of recommendations from the independent review, including:

  • Introducing a transparent, merit-based appointment process for commissioners, with stronger conflict of interest requirements;
  • Separating the Residential Tenancy Office from IRAC and updating residential tenancy and appeal processes;
  • Establishing an Electricity Consumer Advocate to represent consumers and small businesses in major utility proceedings;
  • Supporting the development of performance-based electricity regulations; and
  • Strengthening public reporting and accountability, including regular independent reviews of the new Commission. 

Once these initial changes are made and legislation is in place, it will enable the next stage of renewal will include long-term electricity planning, modernizing the appeals processes, and reviewing land-use and lands protections policies. Ongoing consultation with the public and stakeholders will continue, and many of these modernizations will require future legislative amendments once the new boards are established.

A central pillar to building the new boards will be ensuring services are maintained for Islanders and industry and supporting the continuity of existing applications and proceedings. The government has taken immediate steps to ensure continuity of services while beginning to plan the transition to the new boards including commissioner recruitment, staffing, and transition planning.     

Government will share regular progress updates on the transition planning to the public.                                                 

The final report of the Independent Review of IRAC and government’s response is available here.

 

Media contact:
Sydney Gallant
Office of the Premier
sydngallant@gov.pe.ca 

Background Information: 

Independent Review of Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission: 

  • Commissioner Francis released his interim report on September 18, 2026. In response, government announced plans to introduce legislation to dismantle IRAC’s existing structure and establish two specialized boards during the Fall 2026 Legislative Session. 
  • The final report contains 74 recommendations addressing governance, regulatory oversight, residential tenancies, appeals, electricity regulation and land-use matters.

Key Highlights of the Appeals, Land and Regulatory Commission of Prince Edward Island Act:

Creates two specialized boards, each with dedicated commissioners:

  • The PEI Energy and Utilities Board will regulate electricity, petroleum pricing and other utilities, with a stronger mandate for electricity system planning and oversight so that reliability, including peak winter demand, is planned for rather than reacted to.
  • The PEI Land and Appeals Board will oversee the Lands Protection Act and hear planning and other appeals, with greater transparency around land purchases and clearer rules for who can bring a planning appeal.
  • A shared administrative and technical tribunal will provide common staff and services to both boards, keeping costs down while allowing each board to focus on its own expertise.

Merit-based, accountable appointments:

  • An open, public, merit-based process for appointing commissioners, matched to defined competency requirements.
  • An independent, external recruitment committee to assess candidates.
  • Fixed, defined terms and mandatory performance reviews for all commissioners.

Provides greater transparency:

  • The new Commission shall submit to the Minister an annual report on the activities of the Commission and the Minister shall promptly table the report before the Legislative Assembly. 
  • A mandatory independent review of the regulatory system every six years, so Islanders won’t wait 35 years to find out whether it is still working.

Other Companion Legislation being implemented: 

  • Performance Based Regulations- To require the regulator to tie earnings, rewards and penalties to results Islanders care about: reliability, affordability, service quality, safety, efficiency and lower emissions. 
  • Electricity Consumer Advocate - To designate an advocate to speak for households and small businesses when electricity matters come before the regulator and help Islanders understand electricity issues.
  • Residential Tenancy Act - To provide a clearer and stronger Residential Tenancy Office, so landlords and tenants are never confused with where to take their concerns and to improve the appeal and review process.

item.title: Investigator appointed to lead independent review of Carr case
item.description:
Investigator appointed to lead independent review of Carr case jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/18/2026 - 15:09

An investigator has been appointed to lead an independent review of the Byron Carr murder investigation.

The Honorable Duncan R. Beveridge has been appointed as an investigator under the Police Act. 

"The resulting report and recommendations from this review will be delivered to me and subsequently be made public. It is important to be clear that the review is not to determine liability. It will focus on ensuring police and prosecutorial practices follow best practices for major crime investigations.”

- Justice and Public Safety Minister Bloyce Thompson 

Justice Beveridge is a retired justice of the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal. Prior to his appointment to the bench, he practiced law as a crown prosecutor and defence lawyer. In addition, he has experience in carrying out independent reviews, as part of the Westray prosecution in Nova Scotia and then as senior counsel for the review of the Government of Nova Scotia’s response to reports of institutional abuse.

“I have committed to Justice Beveridge that his review will be completely independent, and he will have the resources he considers necessary to fulfill his mandate,” said Minister Thompson. “That said, if he concludes additional powers are warranted, he can submit an interim report to me with recommendations to that end.”

The review will begin January 4, 2027 and is expected to take several months to a year.

 

Media contact:
Katie Cudmore 
Department of Justice and Public Safety 
Katiecudmore@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder:

Terms of reference for Justice Beveridge’s investigation

Purpose 

The purpose of this appointment is to:  

  • review the circumstances and handling of the Byron Carr homicide investigation conducted by the Charlottetown Police Service, including file management and oversight, evidence and asset management, inter-agency coordination, as well as interaction and consultation with Crown services;  
  • review the operation and administration of the Charlottetown Police Service as a police department in relation to modern policing standards and expectations for Prince Edward Island for major case file investigations; and 
  • make findings regarding the Byron Carr homicide investigation conducted by the Charlottetown Police Service, as well as standards and expectations for major case file police investigations in Prince Edward Island. 

Responsibilities  

The investigation undertaken as a result of the appointment shall be conducted pursuant to section 4 of the Police Act to:  

  • review investigation management, oversight, inter-agency coordination, and interactions with Crown services, regarding the Byron Carr homicide investigation by Charlottetown Police Services, including relevant factors, decisions, policies, practices or biases that may have affected service delivery, investigative outcomes, or public confidence; and 
  • review modern policing standards and expectations for Prince Edward Island regarding major case file investigations, including minimum standards, policies and procedures for 
  • case management investigative practices;  
  • the creation, maintenance, retention, accessibility, and disclosure of investigative files and records;  
  • the collection, handling, storage, tracking, disclosure, retention, and disposition of evidence; 
  • evidence continuity and chain of custody;  
  • exhibit, property, and evidence management systems and controls; 
  • inter-agency coordination and Crown services interaction; 
  • organizational governance; 
  • supervision, accountability, leadership and oversight; and 
  • training and development. 

Report 

Upon completion of the investigation the investigator shall, pursuant to section 4(4) of the Act, prepare and submit a written report to the Minister, which shall include the investigator’s findings. 

The investigator’s report will be released to the public subject only to legal and privacy considerations.

item.title: Government’s Response to the Independent IRAC Review
item.description:
Government’s Response to the Independent IRAC Review tlpeters Wed, 11/18/2026 - 10:36

Building a modern, transparent, and accountable regulatory system for Prince Edward Island

The Government of Prince Edward Island is moving forward with building a modern, transparent, and accountable regulatory environment to replace the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission (IRAC), following an independent review led by Commissioner Rory Francis.

The review resulted in 74 recommendations to improve regulatory services, strengthen accountability and modernize how decisions are made.

Government will do this through legislative reform, developing policies with the input from Islanders, industries, and stakeholders, and standing up and operationalizing a new regulatory structure with two specialized boards: the PEI Energy and Utilities Board and the PEI Land and Appeals Board. The two boards will be supported by a shared administrative body called the Appeals, Land and Regulatory Commission of Prince Edward Island.      

Why is IRAC changing?

IRAC makes decisions and provides services that affect Islanders in several areas, including electricity rates, residential tenancies, land-related matters and appeals.

The independent review examined IRAC’s structure, responsibilities and operations, and identified opportunities to strengthen transparency, accountability and the delivery of regulatory services.

In September 2026, in response to the interim report that was made public by the independent review, government announced plans to replace IRAC with two specialized regulatory boards.

The proposed changes are intended to provide more focused regulatory oversight, clearer responsibilities and stronger accountability while protecting independent decision-making.

What is changing?

Government is moving forward with legislation to establish two specialized regulatory boards and to create a standalone tenancy office.

  • PEI Energy and Utilities Board
    • This board will be responsible for energy and utilities regulation, including electricity matters.
  • PEI Land and Appeals Board
    • This board will be responsible for land-related regulatory matters and appeals.

The boards would share administrative and technical services to support their operations while maintaining independent decision-making.

  • Residential Tenancy Office
    • The Residential Tenancy Office will operate separately from the regulatory boards. Additional changes are intended to improve residential tenancy processes and appeals. 

What will these changes mean for Islanders?

The reforms are intended to improve regulatory services and make processes clearer and more accountable. This will include: 

  • For tenants and landlords:
    • Clearer responsibilities and improvements to how residential tenancy matters and appeals are handled.
  • For electricity customers:
    • Stronger independent consumer representation in electricity rate hearings and further work to modernize electricity regulation to make utilities more accountable to the customers who pay for their services.
  • For businesses and communities:
    • More specialized regulatory oversight, stronger accountability and improved transparency around decisions that affect Islanders.

Existing regulatory processes and appeals will continue while the transition is planned and implemented.

How will the changes happen?

Government is advancing the recommendations made by the independent review of the Island Regulatory & Appeals Commission, focusing on three main streams of work:     

#1 Legislative reforms

Initially, legislative reforms will focus on establishing the new regulatory structure and strengthening accountability through legislation.

This includes:

  • Establishing the PEI Energy and Utilities Board and PEI Land and Appeals Board, supported by shared administrative and technical services. 
  • Introducing a transparent, merit-based appointment process for commissioners, with stronger conflict of interest requirements.
  • Separating the Residential Tenancy Office from IRAC and updating residential tenancy and appeal processes.
  • Establishing an Office of the Independent Consumer Advocate to represent consumers and small businesses in major utility proceedings. 
  • Supporting the development of performance-based electricity regulations.
  • Strengthening public reporting and accountability, including regular independent reviews. 

Some legislation has already been tabled and will be debated before the end of 2026.  Additional legislative amendments and changes will be required as the new Commission is established, operational procedures are determined, and policy work is completed to ensure the new Commission can work efficiently and effectively to serve Islanders.     

#2 Policy Development & Ongoing Public Consultation     

Some recommendations require additional review, planning or consultation before further decisions are made and the recommendations can be operationalized under the new structure.

This work includes:

  • Long-term electricity planning;
  • Modernizing appeals processes; and
  • Reviewing land-use and land protection policies.   

Government is committed to ongoing consultation on policy development to ensure that those impacted by the changes have an opportunity to provide input. The goal is to ensure that while modernizing policies, procedures, and processes relate to the new regulatory bodies that it provides more accountability, more transparency, and more efficiently under for the people it serves.     

#3: Operationalizing the new Boards and ensuring a smooth transition     

A central pillar to building the new Boards will be ensuring services are maintained for Islanders and industry while supporting the continuity of existing applications and proceedings. This will require significant work to ensure there are no gaps in service delivery and that the new Boards are able to operate under the new model smoothly.   

This work includes:

  • Recruiting and appointing commissioners.
  • Planning staffing and administrative arrangements.
  • Establishing shared services and governance agreements.
  • Preparing budgets, technology and operational systems.
  • Supporting the continued delivery of regulatory services throughout the transition.

Work is advancing in all three work streams and will continue throughout and after the transition period. 

What happens to the 74 recommendations?

Commissioner Francis’s final report contains 74 recommendations covering regulatory services, governance, accountability and other areas of reform.

Government has reviewed the recommendations and identified actions to address the findings.

Some recommendations are being advanced through the workstreams mentioned above. Others fall within the responsibilities of independent regulatory bodies, some of which will require further policy review and consultation with Islanders. Government will act on all recommendations that they are responsible for at the appropriate time before, during, or after the transition period.   

The three work streams provide a framework for moving this work forward while recognizing that different recommendations require different actions and timelines.

Read government’s announcement outlining the legislation being introduced and the next steps in responding to the independent IRAC review.

item.title: November 16-20 is Financial Literacy Week
item.description:
November 16-20 is Financial Literacy Week jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/17/2026 - 15:43

Students across Prince Edward Island will benefit from a strengthened framework aimed at improving financial literacy.

To mark Financial Literacy Week, the province has created a Provincial K-12 Literacy Framework to help Island students build the confidence and practical skills needed to make informed financial decisions throughout their lives. The Framework will help students explore real-world topics such as spending, saving, goal setting, and the factors that influence financial choices.

"Financial literacy is a foundational life skill that helps people make informed decisions and build confidence in managing their financial future. Through the Provincial K-12 Financial Literacy Framework, we are ensuring students have opportunities to develop these skills throughout their education, helping prepare them for success in school, work and life."

- Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

The Framework was used to develop a Financial Literacy Week Activity Guide, which offers engaging, age-appropriate learning opportunities for students across Island schools. The guide is available as an internal resource for Island educators to use in their lesson plans during Financial Literacy Week and throughout the school year.

This year marks the first time the Government of Prince Edward Island has formally recognized Financial Literacy Week, which will take place annually during the third full week of November.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
